content: {"entries":[{"revises":[],"knowledge":[{"text":"The installed Skill directed applying heat/cool by holding the object and invoking `heat`/`cool` with the appliance, warning against putting the object into the appliance and toggling its door. In the heat-egg task (train:0028) the parent moved egg 1 into the microwave (P9:14) and then alternated open/close (P9:16 through P9:50) without ever applying heat, ending at the 50-step limit, whereas the candidate held the egg and used `heat egg 1 with microwave 1` (Q9:7) and placed it on countertop 1 (Q9:9) in a 9-step success. In the heat-mug task (train:0029) the parent likewise inserted mug 4 into the microwave (P10:45) and toggled it (P10:46, P10:50) to the step limit, while the candidate used hold-based heat (Q10:39) but still failed because it had taken a cup rather than the required mug (Q10:25) and never placed it. Among the ten current candidate runs, none inserted an object into the microwave/fridge to apply a state change and then toggled the door; the toggling failure mode appeared only in these parent runs. Because the whole Skill was installed as one joint edit, this supports the targeted hold-based behavior but does not isolate its contribution to whole-task success.","evidence":["diff","P9:14","P9:16","P9:50","Q9:7","Q9:9","P10:45","P10:46","P10:50","Q10:39","Q10:25"]},{"text":"Where a candidate acquired an object matching the task noun and applied the required transformation while holding it, the prescribed transform-then-place sequence was completed. Clean-spoon (train:0020): the candidate cleaned spoon 1 with sinkbasin 1 (Q1:8) and moved it to diningtable 1 (Q1:10), matching the parent's clean/place sequence but taking 10 steps versus the parent's 9 because it first detoured to countertop 1 (Q1:1). Cool-bread (train:0022, train:0023): candidates cooled bread 1 with fridge 1 (Q3:7, Q4:6) then moved it to countertop 1 (Q3:9, Q4:8). Hot-apple (train:0027): the candidate applied `heat apple 1 with microwave 1` while the microwave was still closed (Q8:4 states it is closed, Q8:5 heats successfully) then moved the apple to fridge 1 (Q8:8), whereas the parent opened the microwave first (P8:11, P8:12); both succeeded, so opening the appliance was not required for applying heat in that instance. These successes preserve the acquire-transform-place capability but, given the joint edit, do not show that the search clauses caused them.","evidence":["diff","P1:5","P1:7","P1:9","Q1:1","Q1:8","Q1:10","P3:8","Q3:7","Q3:9","P4:45","Q4:6","Q4:8","P8:11","P8:12","Q8:4","Q8:5","Q8:8"]},{"text":"The search/coverage and anti-revisit clauses had mixed associations, and attribution is limited because search order is a free choice under the joint edit. Efficiency gains: in cool-bread (train:0023) the candidate reached diningtable 1, took bread 1 (Q4:4), cooled it (Q4:6) and placed it (Q4:8) in 8 steps, while the parent wandered and reached that same diningtable only at P4:41 before finishing in 47 steps; in hot-apple (train:0027) the candidate reached diningtable 1 by its second step (Q8:2) and finished in 8 steps versus the parent's 14 after additional refrigerator and shelf checks (P8:8). Regressions to parent-success/candidate-failure: in cool-plate (train:0025) the parent opened cabinet 9, took plate 1 (P6:37, P6:38), cooled it (P6:40) and moved it to diningtable 1 (P6:43) in 43 steps, while the candidate never reached cabinet 9 within its 50 steps and repeatedly cycled countertop 1/2, cabinet 1/2 and drawer 1/2 (Q6:50); in cool-pot (train:0026) the parent took pot 2 from stoveburner 4 and finished in 20 steps (P7:16, P7:18, P7:20) while the candidate reached pot 2 only at Q7:49 and was cut off at Q7:50 after extensive revisiting. Both sides failed with heavy re-checking in cool-bread (train:0021) and cool-pan (train:0024). The guidance therefore did not ensure coverage of unvisited candidate locations or stop recheck loops, and candidates still revisited known-empty locations.","evidence":["diff","Q4:4","Q4:6","Q4:8","P4:41","Q8:2","P8:8","P6:37","P6:38","P6:40","P6:43","Q6:50","P7:16","P7:18","P7:20","Q7:49","Q7:50","P2:34","Q2:16","P5:13","Q5:23"]},{"text":"In several runs the agent operated on an object whose type did not match the task noun, contrary to the object-selection clause, and the recovery clause did not redirect it. In cool-pot (train:0026) the candidate took pan 1 from stoveburner 2 (Q7:7) and moved it to stoveburner 1 (Q7:8) although the task required a pot, and located the matching pot 2 only at Q7:49 near the step limit. In heat-mug (train:0029) the candidate took cup 1 (Q10:25) and applied heat to it (Q10:39, Q10:44) although the task required a mug, and never placed it. In cool-pan (train:0024) the parent repeatedly took and repositioned pot 1 on stoveburner 1 (P5:28, P5:29, P5:32, P5:36) although the task required a pan, without task progress. No current run shows an agent correcting a wrong-type choice toward the matching object before its step budget ran out, so the type-matching/recovery guidance is not evidenced as effective here.","evidence":["diff","Q7:7","Q7:8","Q7:49","Q10:25","Q10:39","Q10:44","P5:28","P5:29","P5:32","P5:36"]},{"text":"Parent runs frequently contained malformed or non-admissible actions, including empty strings and placeholder/reasoning text (for example P2:1, P2:6, P3:5, P4:4, P4:28, P5:5, P5:30, P6:16, P6:20, P9:6, P9:21), whereas candidate runs emitted no empty-string, ellipsis, or embedded-reasoning actions. Candidate compliance was still imperfect: candidates issued navigation commands that were not in the current admissible list (Q6:6 and Q6:23 'go to cabinet 3'; Q5:17 and Q7:17 'go to stoveburner 2'), and Q10:33 was recorded with a 'missing_action_tag' fallback. The single-verbatim-admissible-command clause is thus associated with eliminating the gross malformed-action pattern but not with perfect admissibility.","evidence":["diff","P2:1","P2:6","P3:5","P4:4","P4:28","P5:5","P5:30","P6:16","P6:20","P9:6","P9:21","Q6:6","Q6:23","Q5:17","Q7:17","Q10:33"]}]}]}
